verses.text: This Jesus was the son of Sirach, and grand-childe to Jesus of the same name with him; This man therefore lived in the latter times, after the people had been led away captiue, and called home again, and almost after all the Prophets. Now his grandfather Jesus (as he himself witnesseth) was a man of great diligence and wisedome among the Hebrewes, who did not only gather the graue and short Sentences of wise men, that had been before him, but himself also vttered some of his own, full of much understanding and wisedome. When as therefore the first Jesus died, leauing this book almost perfected, Si rach his son receiuing it after him, left it to his own son Jesus, who hauing gotten it into his hands, compiled it all orderly into one Volume, and called it Wisdom, Intituling it, both by his own name, his fathers name, and his grandfathers, alluring the hearer by the very name of Wisedome, to have a greater love to the studie of this Book. It conteineth therefore wise Sayings, darke Sentences, and Parables, and certain particular ancient godly stories of men that pleased Alahayam. Also his Prayer and Song. Moreouer, what benefits Alahayam had vouchsafed his people, and what plagues he had heaped on their enemies. This Jesus did imitate Solomon, and was no lesse famous for Wisedome, and learning, both being indeed a man of great learning, and so reputed also. Whereas many and great things have been deliuered to us by the Law and the Prophets, and by others that have followed their steps, for the which things Yahsharala ought to be commended for learning and Wisedome, and whereof not only the Readers must needs become skilful themselues, but also they that desire to learne, be able to profit them which are without, both by speaking and writing : My grandfather Jesus, when he had much given himself to the reading of the Law, and the Prophets, and other Books of our fathers, and had gotten in it good judgment, was drawen on also himself, to write something pertayning to learning and Wisedome, to the intent that those which are desirous to learne, and are addicted to these things, might profit much more in living according to the Law. Therefore, let me intreat you to reade it with favor and attention, and to pardon Us, in which we may secme to come short of some words which we have laboured to interprete. For the same things vttered in Hebrew, and translated into an other tongue, have not the same force in them : and not only these things, but the Law it self, and the Prophets, and the rest of the Books, have no small difference, when they are spoken in their own language. For in the eight and thirtieth yeere comming into Egypt, when Euergetes was King, and continuing there some time, I found a Book of no small learning, therefore I thought it most necessary for mee, to bestow some diligence and trauaile to interprete it: Vsing great watchfulnesse, and skill in that space, to bring the Book to an end, and set it foorth for them also, which in a strange country are willing to learne, being prepared before in maners to line after the Law. All wisedome commeth from the Lord, and is with him for ever.
Who can number the sand of the sea, and the drops of raine, and the days of eternity?
Who can finde out the height of heaven, and the breadth of the earth, and the deepe, and wisedome?
Wisedome has been created before all things, and the understanding of prudence from euerlasting.
The word of Alahayam most high, is the fountaine of wisdom, & her ways are euerlasting commandements.
To whom has the root of wisdom been reuealed? or who has knowen her wise counsels?
There is one wise and greatly to be feared; the Lord sitting on his Throne.
He created her, and saw her, and numbred her, and powred her out on all his workes.
She with all flesh according to his gift, and he has given her to them that love him.
The fear of the Lord is honour, and glory, and gladnesse, and a crowne of reioycing.
The fear of the Lord makes a merrie heart, and gives ioy and gladnesse, and a long life.
Who so feareth the Lord, it shall goe well with him at the last, & he shall finde favor in the day of his death.
To fear the Lord, is the beginning of wisedome: and it was created with the faithfull in the wombe.
She has built an euerlasting foundation with men, and she shall continue with their seede.
To fear the Lord, is fulnesse of wisedome, and filleth men with her fruits.
She filleth all their house with things desireable, and the garners with her increase.
The fear of the Lord is a crowne of wisedome, making peace and perfect health to flourish, both which are the gifts of Alahayam: and it enlargeth their reioycing that love him.
Wisedome raineth down skill and knowledge of understanding, and exalteth them to honour that holde her fast.
The root of wisedome is to fear the Lord, and the branches of it are long life.
The fear of the Lord driueth away sins: and where it is present, it turneth away wrath.
A furious man cannot be justified, for the sway of his fury shall be his destruction.
A patient man will beare for a time, and afterward ioy shall spring up to him.
He wil hide his words for a time, and the lippes of many shall declare his wisedome.
The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisedome: but godlines is an abomination to a sinner.
If you desire wisedome, keepe the commaundements, and the Lord shall give her to you.
For the fear of the Lord is wisdom, and instruction: and faith and meekenesse are his delight.
Distrust not the fear of the Lord when you are poore: and come not to him with a double heart.
Be not an hypocrite in the sight of men, and take good heede what you speakest.

Exalt not your self, lest you fall, and bring dishonor on your soule, and so Alahayam discouer your secrets, and cast you down in the midst of the congregation, because you camest not in truth, to the fear of the Lord: but your heart is full of deceit.
My son, if you come to serve the Lorde, prepare your soule for temptation.
Set your heart aright, and constantly endure, and make not haste in time of trouble.
Cleaue to him, and depart not away, that you mayest be increased at your last end.
Whatsoeuer is brought on you, take cheerefully, and be patient when you are changed to a lowe estate.
For gold is tried in the fire, and acceptable men in the furnace of aduersitie.
Believe in him, and he will helpe you, order your way aright, and trust in him.
You that fear the Lord, waite for his mercie, and goe not aside, lest you fall.
You that fear the Lord, believe him, and your reward shall not faile.
You that fear the Lord, hope for good, and for euerlasting ioy and mercy.
Looke at the generations of old, and see, did ever any trust in the Lord, and was confounded? or did any abide in his fear, & was forsaken? or whom did he ever despise, that called on him?
For the Lord is full of compassion, and mercie, longsuffering, and very pitifull, and forgiueth sins, and saueth in time of affliction.
Woe be to fearefull hearts, and faint hands, and the sinner that goes two ways.
Woe to him that is faint hearted, for he beleeueth not, therefore shall he not be defended.
Woe to you that have lost patience: and what will you do when the Lord shall visite you?
They that fear the Lord, will not disobey his word, and they that love him, will keepe his ways.
They that fear the Lord, will seeke that which is well pleasing to him, and they that love him, shall be filled with the Law.
They that fear the Lord, will prepare their hearts, and humble their soules in his sight:
Saying, We will fal into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men: for as his maiestie is, so is his mercie.
Heare mee your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.
For the Lord has given the father honour over the children, and has confirmed the authoritie of the mother over the sons.
Who so honoureth his father, makes an atonement for his sins.
And he that honoureth his mother, is as one that layeth up treasure.
Who so honoureth his father, shall have ioy of his own children, and when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.
He that honoureth his father, shall have a long life, and he that is obedient to the Lord, shall be a comfort to his mother.
He that feareth the Lord, will honour his father, and will do seruice to his parents, as to his masters.
Honour your father and mother, both in word and deed, that a blessing may come on you from them.
For the blessing of the father establisheth the houses of children, but the curse of the mother rooteth out foundations.
Glory not in the dishonour of your father, for your fathers dishonour is no glory to you.
For the glory of a man, is from the honour of his father, and a mother in dishonour, is a reproch to the children.
My son, helpe your father in his age, and grieue him not as long as he liueth.
And if his understanding faile, have patience with him, and despise him not, when you are in your ful strength.
For the relieuing of your father shall not be forgotten: and in stead of sins it shall be added to build you up.
In the day of your affliction it shall be remembred, your sins also shall melt away, as the yce in þ faire warme weather.
He that forsaketh his father, is as a blasphemer, and he that angreth his mother, is cursed of Alahayam.
My son, goe on with your businesse in meekenesse, so will you be beloued of him that is approued.
The greater you are, the more humble your self, and you will find favor before the Lord.
Many are in high place and of renowne: but mysteries are reueiled to the meeke.
For the power of the Lord is great, and he is honoured of the lowly.
Seeke not out the things that are too hard for you, neither search the things that are above your strength.
But what is commaunded you, thinke thereupon with reuerence, for it is not needfull for you, to see with your eyes, the things that are in secret.
Be not curious in vnnecessarie matters: for moe things are showed to you, then men understand.
For many are deceiued by their own vaine opinion, and an evil suspition has ouerthrowen their judgment.
Without eyes you will want light: professe not the knowledge therfore that you have not.
A stubborne heart shall fare evil at the last, and he that loueth danger shall perish in it.
An obstinate heart shall be laden with sorrowes, and the wicked man shall heape sin on sin.
In the punishment of the proud there is no remedie: for the plant of wickednesse has taken roote in him.
The heart of the prudent will understand a parable, and an attentiue eare is the desire of a wise man.
Water will quench a flaming fire, and almes makes an attonement for sins.
And he that requiteth good turnes, is mindfull of that which may come heereafter: and when he falleth he shall find a stay.
My son, defraude not the poore of his living, and make not the needy eies to waite long.
Make not an hungry soule sorrowfull, neither prouoke a man in his distresse.
Adde not more trouble to an heart that is vexed, and deferre not to give to him that is in neede.
Reiect not the supplication of the afflicted, neither turne away your face from a poore man.
Turne not away your eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse you:
For if he curse you in the bitternesse of his soule, his prayer shall be heard of him that made him.
Get your self the love of the congregation, and bow your head to a great man.
Let it not grieue you to bowe down your eare to the poore, and give him a friendly answere with meekenesse.
Deliuer him that suffreth wrong, from the hand of the oppressour, and be not faint hearted when you sittest in judgment.
Be as a father to the fatherlesse, and in stead of a husband to their mother, so will you be as the son of the most high, and he shall love you more then your mother does.
Wisedome exalteth her children, and layeth hold of them that seeke her.
He that loueth her, loueth life, and they that seeke to her earely, shall be filled with ioy.
He that holdeth her fast shall inherit glory, and wheresoeuer she entreth, the Lord will blesse.
They that serve her shall minister to the Holy one, and them that love her, the Lord does love.
Who so gives eare to her, shall judge the nations, and he that attendeth to her, shall dwell securely.
If a man commit himself to her, he shall inherite her, and his generation shall hold her in possession.
For at the first she will walke with him by crooked ways, and bring fear and dread on him, and torment him with her discipline, until she may trust his soule, and try him by her Lawes.
Then wil she returne the straight way to him, and comfort him, and show him her secrets.
But if he goe wrong, she will forsake him, and give him over to his own ruine.
Obserue the opportunitie, and beware of evil, and be not ashamed when it concerneth your soule.
For there is a shame that bringeth sin, and there is a shame which is glory and grace.
Accept no person against your soule, and let not the reuerence of any man cause you to fall:
And refraine not to speak, when there is occasion to do good, and hide not your wisedome in her beautie.
For by speach wisedome shall be knowen, and learning by the word of the tongue.
In no wise speak against the truth, but be abashed of the errour of your ignorance.
Be not ashamed to confesse your sins, and force not the course of the riuer.
Make not your self an vnderling to a foolish man, neither accept the person of the mighty.
Striue for the truth to death, and the Lord shall fight for you.
Be not hastie in your tongue, and in your deeds slacke and remisse.
Be not as a Lion in your house, nor franticke among your servants.
Let not your hand be stretched out to receive, and shut when you should repay.
Set not your heart on your goods, and say not, I have ynough for my life.
Folow not your own mind, and your strength, to walke in the ways of your heart:
And say not, Who shall controll mee for my workes? for the Lord will surely revenge your pride.
Say not, I have sinned, and what harme has happened to mee? for the Lord is long suffering, he wil in no wise let you goe.
Concerning propitiation, be not without fear to adde sin to sin.
And say not, His mercy is great, he will be pacified for the multitude of my sins: for mercy and wrath come from him, and his indignation resteth on sinners.

Make no tarying to turne to the Lord, and put not off from day to day: for suddenly shall the wrath of the Lord come foorth, and in your securitie you will be destroyed, and perish in the day of vengeance.
Set not your heart on goods vniustly gotten: for they shall not profit you in the day of calamitie.
Winnow not with every winde, and goe not into every way: for so does the sinner that has a double tongue.
Be stedfast in your understanding, and let your word be the same.
Be swift to heare, and let your life be sincere, & with patience give answere.
If you have understanding, answer your neighbour, if not, lay your hand on your mouth.
Honour and shame is in talke; and the tongue of man is his fall.
Be not called a whisperer, and lye not in wait with your tongue: for a foule shame is on the thiefe, and an evil condemnation on the double tongue.
Be not ignorant of any thing, in a great matter or a small.
In stead of a friend, become not an enemie; for you will inherite an ill name, shame, and reproch: even so shall a sinner that has a double tongue.
Extoll not your self in the counsell of your own heart, that your soule be not torne in pieces as a bull
You will eat up your leaues, and loose your fruit, and leaue your self as a dry tree.
A wicked soule shall destroy him that has it, and shall make him to be laughed to scorne of his enemies.
Sweet language will multiply friends: and a faire speaking tongue will increase kinde greetings.
Be in peace with many: neuerthelesse have but one counseller of a thousand.
If you wouldst get a friend, proue him first, and be not hasty to credit him.
For some man is a friend for his own occasion, and will not abide in the day of your trouble.
And there is a friend, who being turned to enmitie, and strife, will discouer your reproch.
Again some friend is a companion at the table, and will not continue in the day of your affliction.
But in your prosperitie he will be as your self, and will be bould over your servants.
If you be brought low, he will be against you, and will hide himself from your face.
Separate your self from your enemies, and take heed of your friends.
A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one, has found a treasure.
Nothing does counteruaile a faithful friend, and his excellencie is vnualuable.
A faithfull friend is the medicine of life, and they that fear the Lord shall finde him.
Who so feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright, for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.
My son, gather instruction from your youth up: so will you finde wisedome till your old age.
Come to her as one that ploweth, and soweth, and wait for her good fruits, for you will not toile much in labouring about her, but you will eat of her fruits right soone.
She is very vnpleasant to the vnlearned: he that is without understanding, will not remaine with her.
She wil lye on him as a mightie stone of triall, and he will cast her from him ere it be long.
For wisedome is according to her name, and she is not manifest to many.
Give eare, my son, receive my aduice, and refuse not my counsell,
And put your feet into her fetters, and your necke into her chaine.
Bow down your shoulder, and beare her, and be not grieued with her bonds.
Come to her with your whole heart, and keepe her ways with all your power.
Search and seeke, and she shall be made knowen to you, and when you have got hold of her, let her not goe.
For at the last you will finde her rest, and that shall be turned to your ioy.
Then shall her fetters be a strong defence for you, and her chaines a robe of glory.
For there is a golden ornament on her, and her bandes are purple lace.
You will put her on as a robe of honour: and will put her about you as a crowne of ioy.
My son, if you will, you will be taught: and if you will apply your mind, you will be prudent.
If you love to heare, you will receive understanding: and if you bow your eare, you will be wise.
Stand in the multitude of the elders, and cleaue to him that is wise.
Be willing to heare every godly discourse, and let not the parables of understanding escape you.
And if you seest a man of understanding, get you betimes to him, and let your foote weare the steps of his doore.
Let your mind be on the ordinances of the Lord, & meditate continually in his commandements: he shall establish your heart, and give you wisedome at your own desire.
Do no evil, so shall no harme come to you.
Depart from the vniust, and iniquitie shall turne away from you.
My son, sow not on the furrowes of vnrighteousnesse, and you will not reape them seven folde.
Seeke not of the Lord preheminence, neither of the King the seate of honour.
Iustifie not your self before the Lord, and boast not of your wisedome before the king.
Seeke not to be judge, being not able to take away iniquitie, lest at any time you fear the person of the mightie, and lay a stumbling blocke in the way of your vprightnesse.
Offend not against the multitude of a city, and then you will not cast your self down among the people.
Bind not one sin on another, for in one you will not be vnpunished.
Say not, Alahayam wil looke on the multitude of my oblations, and when I offer to the most High Alahayam, he will accept it.
Be not faint hearted when you makest your prayer, and neglect not to give almes.
Laugh no man to scorne in the bitternesse of his soule: for there is one which humbleth and exalteth.
Deuise not a lie against your brother: neither do the like to your friend.
Use not to make any maner of lie: for the custome of it is not good.
Use not many words in a multitude of Elders, and make not much babling when you prayest.
Hate not laborious worke, neither husbandrie, which the most High has ordeined.
Number not your self among the multitude of sinners, but remember that wrath will not tary long.
Humble your soule greatly: for the vengeance of the ungodly is fire and wormes.
Change not a friend for any good by no meanes: neither a faithfull brother for the gold of Ophir.
Forgoe not a wise and good woman: for her grace is above gold.
Whereas your servant worketh truely, entreate him not evil, nor the hireling that bestoweth himself wholly for you.
Let your soule love a good servant, and defraud him not of liberty.
Have you cattell? have an eye to them, and if they be for your profit, keepe them with you.
Have you children? instruct them, and bow down their necke from their youth.
Have you daughters? have care of their body, and shewe not your self cheerefull toward them.
Marrie your daughter, and so will you have performed a weightie matter: but give her to a man of understanding.
Have you a wife after your mind? forsake her not, but give not your self over to a light woman.
Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrowes of your mother.
Remember that you wast begot of them, and how canst you recompense them the things that they have done for you?
Fear the Lord with all your soule, and reuerence his priests.
Love him that made you with all your strength, and forsake not his ministers.

Fear the Lord, and honour the priest: and give him his portion, as it is commanded you, the first fruits, and the trespasse offering, & the gift of the shoulders, and the sacrifice of sanctification, and the first fruits of the holy things.
And stretch your hand to the poore, that your blessing may be perfected
A gift has grace in the sight of every man living, and for the dead deteine it not.
Faile not to be with them that weepe, and mourne with them that mourne.
Be not slow to visit the sicke: for that shall make you to be beloued.
Whatsoeuer you takest in hand, remember the end, and you will never do amisse.
Striue not with a mighty man, lest you fall into his hands.
Be not at variance with a rich man, lest he ouerweigh you: for gold has destroyed many, and peruerted the hearts of kings.
Striue not with a man that is full of tongue, and heape not wood on his fire.
Iest not with a rude man, lest your ancestours be disgraced.
Reproch not a man that turneth from sin, but remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
Dishonour not a man in his old age: for even some of us waxe old.
Reioice not over your greatest enemie being dead, but remember that we die all.
Despise not the discourse of the wise, but acquaint your self with their prouerbs; for of them you will learne instruction, & how to serve great men with ease.
Misse not the discourse of the Elders: for they also learned of their fathers, and of them you will learne understanding, and to give answere as need requireth.
Kindle not the coales of a sinner, lest you be burnt with the flame of his fire.
Rise not up (in anger) at the presence of an iniurious person, least he lie in waite to entrap you in your words.
Lend not to him that is mightier then your self; for if you lendest him, count it but lost.
Be not surety above your power: for if you be surety, take care to pay it.
Goe not to law with a judge, for they will judge for him according to his honour.
Trauaile not by the way with a bold fellow, least he become grieuous to you: for he will do according to his own will, and you will perish with him through his folly.
Striue not with an angry man, and goe not with him into a solitary place: for blood is as nothing in his sight, and where there is no helpe, he will ouerthrow you.
Consult not with a foole; for he cannot keepe counsell.
Do no secret thing before a stranger, for you know not what he will bring forth.
Open not your heart to every man, least he requite you with a shrewd turne.
Be not iealous over the wife of your bosome, and teach her not an euil lesson against your self.
Give not your soule to a woman, to set her foot on your substance.
Meete not with an harlot, least you fall into her snares.
Use not much the companie of a woman that is a singer, least you be taken with her attempts.
Gaze not on a maide, that you fall not by those things, that are pretious in her.
Give not your soule to harlots, that you loose not your inheritance.
Looke not round about you, in the streets of the city, neither wander you in the solitary places of it.
Turne away your eye from a beautifull woman, and looke not on anothers beautie: for many have been deceiued by the beautie of a woman, for heerewith love is kindled as a fire.

Sit not at all with another mans wife, nor sit down with her in your armes, and spend not your money with her at the wine, least your heart incline to her, and so thorough your desire you fall into destruction.
Forsake not an old friend, for the new is not comparable to him: a new friend is as new wine: when it is old, you will drinke it with pleasure.
Enuy not the glory of a sinner: for you know not what shall be his end.
Delight not in the thing that the ungodly have pleasure in, but remember they shall not goe vnpunished to their graue.

Keepe you farre from the man that has power to kill, so will you not doubt the fear of death: and if you come to him, make no fault, least he take away your life presently: remember that you goest in the midst of snares, and that you walkest on the battlements of the city.
As neere as you canst, ghesse at your neighbour, and consult with the wise.
Let your talke be with the wise, and all your communication in the law of the most high.
And let just men eate and drinke with you, and let your glorying be in the fear of the Lord.
For the hand of the artificer, the worke shall be commended: and the wise ruler of the people, for his speech.
A man of an ill tongue is dangerous in his city, and he that is rash in his talke shall be hated.
A wise judge will instruct his people, & the gouernement of a prudent man is well ordered.
As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers, and what maner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell in it.
An vnwise king destroyeth his people, but through the prudence of them which are in authoritie, the city shall be inhabited.
The power of the earth is in the hand of the Lord, and in due time he will set over it one that is profitable.
In the hand of Alahayam is the prosperitie of man: and on the person of the scribe shall he lay his honour.
Beare not hatred to your neighbour for every wrong, and do nothing at all by iniurious practises.
Pride is hatefull before Alahayam, and man: and by both does one commit iniquitie.
Because of vnrighteous dealings, iniuries, and riches got by deceit, the kingdome is translated from one people to another.
Why is earth and ashes proude? There is not a more wicked thing, then a couetous man: for such an one setteth his own soule to sale, because while he liueth, he casteth away his bowels.
The Phisition cutteth off a long disease, and he that is to day a King, to morrow shall die.
For when a man is dead, he shall inherite creeping things, beastes and wormes.
The beginning of pride is, when one departeth from Alahayam, and his heart is turned away from his maker.
For pride is the beginning of sin, and he that has it, shall powre out abomination: and therefore the Lord brought on them strange calamities, and ouerthrew them vtterly.
The Lord has cast down the thrones of proud Princes, and set up the meeke in their stead.
The Lord has plucked up the rootes of the proud nations: and planted the lowly in their place.
The Lord ouerthrew countreys of the heathen: and destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
He tooke some of them away, and destroyed them, and has made their memoriall to cease from the earth.
Pride was not made for men, nor furious anger for them that are borne of a woman.

They that fear the Lord are a sure seed, and they that love him, an honourable plant: they that regard not the Law, are a dishonourable seed, they that transgresse the commandements, are a deceiuable seed.
Among brothers he that is chiefe is honourable, so are they that fear the Lord in his eyes.
The fear of the Lord goes before the obtayning of authoritie: but roughnesse and pride, is the loosing of it.
Whether he be rich, noble, or poore, their glory is the fear of the Lord.
It is not meet to despise the poore man that has understanding, neither is it conuenient to magnifie a sinnefull man.
Great men, and Iudges, and Potentates shall be honoured, yet is there none of them greater then he that feareth the Lord.
Unto the servant that is wise, shall they that are free do seruice: and he that has knowledge, will not grudge when he is reformed.
Be not ouerwise in doing your busines, and boast not your self in the time of your distresse.
Better is he that laboureth and aboundeth in all things, then he that boasteth himself, and wanteth bread.
My son, glorifie your soule in meekenesse, and give it honour according to the dignitie of it.
Who wil iustifie him that sinneth against his own soule? and who will honour him that dishonoureth his own life?
The poore man is honoured for his skill, and the rich man is honoured for his riches.
He that is honoured in pouertie, how much more in riches? And he that is dishonourable in riches, how much more in pouertie?
Wisedome lifteth up the head of him that is of low degree, and makes him to sit among great men.
Commend not a man for his beautie, neither abhorre a man for his outward appearance.
The Be is little among such as flie, but her fruite is the chiefe of sweete things.
Boast not of your cloathing and raiment, and exalt not your self in the day of honour: for the workes of the Lord are wonderfull, and his workes among men are hidden.
Many kings have sit down on the ground, and one that was never thought of, has worne the crowne.
Many mightie men have been greatly disgraced: and the honourable deliuered into other mens hands.
Blame not before you have examined the truth: understand first, and then rebuke.
Answere not, before you have heard the cause: neither interrupt men in the midst of their talke.
Striue not in a matter that concerneth you not: and sit not in judgment with sinners.
My son, meddle not with many matters: for if you meddle much, you will not be innocent: and if you follow after, you will not obtaine, neither will you escape by flying.
There is one that laboureth and takes paines, and makes haste, and is so much the more behinde.
Again, there is another that is slow, and has neede of helpe, wanting abilitie, and full of pouertie, yet the eye of the Lord looked on him for good, and set him up from his low estate,
And lifted up his head from miserie, so that many that saw it, marueiled at him.
Prosperitie and aduersitie, life and death, pouerty and riches, come of the Lord.
Wisedome, knowledge, and understanding of the Lawe, are of the Lord: love, & the way of good workes, are from him.
Errour and darkness had their beginning together with sinners: and evil shall waxe old with them that glory in it.
The gift of the Lord remaineth with the godly, and his favor bringeth prosperitie for ever.
There is that waxeth rich by his warinesse, and pinching, and this is the portion of his reward:
Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eate continually of my goods, and yet he knows not what time shall come on him, and that he must leaue those things to others, and die.
Be stedfast in your couenant, and be conuersant in it, and waxe old in your worke.
Marueile not at the workes of sinners, but trust in the Lord, and abide in your labour: for it is an easie thing in the sight of the Lord, on the sudden to make a poore man rich.
The blessing of the Lord is in the reward of the godly, and suddenly he makes his blessing to flourish.
Say not, what profit is there of my seruice? and what good things shall I have hereafter?
Again, say not, I have enough, and possesse many things; and what evil can come to me hereafter?
In the day of prosperitie, there is a forgetfulnesse of affliction: and in the day of affliction, there is no remembrance of prosperitie.
For it is an easie thing to the Lord in the day of death, to reward a man according to his ways.
The affliction of an houre, makes a man forget pleasure: and in his end, his deeds shall be discouered.
Judge none blessed before his death: for a man shall be knowen in his children.
Bring not every man into your house, for the deceitfull man has many traines.
Like as a Partrich taken in a cage, so is the heart of the proud; and like as a spie, watcheth he for your fall.
For he lieth in wait, and turneth good into evil, and in things worthy praise, will lay blame on you.
Of a sparke of fire, a heape of coales is kindled: and a sinnefull man layeth waite for blood.
Take heed of a mischieuous man, (for he worketh wickednesse) lest he bring on you a perpetuall blot.
Receive a stranger into your house, and he will disturbe you, and turne you out of your own.
When you will do good, know to whō you doest it, so will you be thanked for your benefites.
Do good to the godly man, and you will find a recompence, and if not from him, yet from the most high.
There can no good come to him that is alwayes occupied in evil: nor to him that gives no almes.
Give to the godly man, and helpe not a sinner.

Do well to him that is lowly, but give not to the ungodly: hold backe your bread, and give it not to him, lest he ouermaster you thereby. For you will receive twice as much evil, for all the good you will have done to him.
For the most High hateth sinners, and will repay vengeance to the ungodly, and keepeth them against the mightie day of their punishment.
Give to the good, and helpe not the sinner.
A friend cannot be knowen in prosperitie, and an enemy cannot be hidden in aduersitie.
In the prosperitie of a man, enemies will be grieued, but in his aduersitie, even a friend will depart.
Never trust your enemie: for like as yron rusteth, so is his wickednesse.

Though he humble himself, and goe crouching, yet take good heed, and beware of him, and you will be to him, as if you hadst wiped a looking glasse, and you will knowe that his rust has not been altogether wiped away.

Set him not by you, lest when he has ouerthrowen you, he stand up in your place, neither let him sit at your right hand, lest he seeke to take your seat, and you at the last remember my wordes, and be pricked with it.
Who will pitie a charmer that is bitten with a serpent, or any such as come nigh wilde beasts?
So one that goes to a sinner, and is defiled with him in his sins, who will pitie?
For a while he will abide with you, but if you begin to fall, he wil not tarie.
An enemie speaks sweetly with his lippes, but in his heart he imagineth how to throw you into a pit: he will weepe with his eyes, but if he find opportunitie, he will not be satisfied with blood.
If aduersitie come on you, you will find him there first, & though he pretend to helpe you, yet shall he vndermine you.
He will shake his head and clap his handes, and whisper much, and change his countenance.
He that toucheth pitch, shall be defiled with it, and he that has fellowship with a proude man, shall be like to him.

Burthen not your self above your power, while you liuest, and have no fellowship with one that is mightier, and richer then your self. For how agree the kettle and the earthen pot together? for if the one be smitten against the other, it shall be broken.
The rich man has done wrong, and yet he threatneth withall: the poore is wronged, and he must intreat also.
If you be for his profit, he will use you: but if you have nothing, he will forsake you.
If you have any thing, he will live with you, yea he will make you bare, and will not be sorie for it.
If he have need of you, he will deceiue you, and smile on you, and put you in hope, he will speak you faire, and say, What wantest you?

And he will shame you by his meates, until he have drawen you drie twice or thrice, and at the last he will laugh you to scorne: afterward when he seeth you, he will forsake you, and shake his head at you.
Beware that you be not deceiued, and brought down in your iolitie.
If you be inuited of a mighty man, withdraw your self, and so much the more will he inuite you.
Presse you not on him, lest you be put backe, stand not farre off, lest you be forgotten.
Affect not to be made equall to him in talke, and believe not his many words: for with much communication will he tempt you, and smiling on you will get out your secrets.
But cruelly he will lay up your words, and will not spare to do you hurt, and to put you in prison.
Obserue and take good heed, for you walkest in peril of your ouerthrowing: when you hearest these things, awake in your sleepe.
Love the Lord all your life, and call on him for your salvation.
Every beast loueth his like, and every man loueth his neighbour.
All flesh consorteth according to kind, and a man will cleaue to his like:
What fellowship has the wolfe with the lambe? so the sinner with the godly.
What agreement is there between the Hyena and a dogge? and what peace between the rich and the poore?
As the wilde asse is the lyons pray in the wildernesse: so the rich eate up the poore.
As the proud hate humilitie: so does the rich abhorre the poore.
A rich man beginning to fall, is held up of his friends: but a poore man being down, is thrust also away by his friends.

When a rich man is fallen, he has many helpers: he speaks things not to be spoken, and yet men iustifie him: the poore man slipt, and yet they rebuked him too: he spake wisely, and could have no place.

When a rich man speaks, every man holdeth his tongue, and looke what he sayeth, they extoll it to the clouds: but if the poore man speak, they say, What fellow is this? and if he stumble, they will helpe to ouerthrowe him.
Riches are good to him that has no sin, and pouerty is evil in the mouth of the ungodly.
The heart of a man changeth his countenance, whether it be for good or evil: and a merry heart makes a cheerefull countenance.
A cheerefull countenance is a token of a heart that is in prosperity, and the finding out of parables, is a wearisome labour of the mind.
Blessed is the man that has not slipt with his mouth, and is not pricked with the multitude of sins.
Blessed is he whose conscience has not condemned him, and who is not fallen from his hope in the Lord.
Riches are not comely for a niggard: and what should an enuious man do with money?
He that gathereth by defrauding his own soule, gathereth for others, that shall spend his goods riotously.
He that is evil to himself, to whom will he be good? he shall not take pleasure in his goods.
There is none worse then he that enuieth himself; and this is a recompence of his wickednesse.
And if he does good, he does it vnwillingly, and at the last he will declare his wickednesse.
The enuious man has a wicked eye, he turneth away his face and despiseth men.
A couetous mans eye is not satisfied with his portion, and the iniquity of the wicked dryeth up his soule.
A wicked eye enuieth bread, and he is a niggard at his table.
My son, according to your habilitie do good to your self, and give the Lord his due offering.
Remember that death will not be long in comming, and that the couenant of the graue is not showed to you.
Do good to your friend before you die, and according to your abilitie, stretch out your hand and give to him.
Defraud not your self of the good day, and let not the part of a good desire ouerpasse you.
Will you not leaue your trauailes to another? and your labours to be diuided by lot?
Give, and take, and sanctifie your soule, for there is no seeking of dainties in the graue.
All flesh waxeth old as a garment: for the couenant from the beginning is; you will die the death.
As of the greene leaues on a thicke tree, some fall, and some grow; so is the generation of flesh and blood, one commeth to an end, and another is borne.
Every worke rotteth and consumeth away, and the worker therof shall goe withall.
Blessed is the man that does meditate good things in wisdom, and that reasoneth of holy things by his understanding.
He that considereth her ways in his heart, shall also have understanding in her secrets.
Goe after her as one that traceth, and lie in wait in her ways.
He that prieth in at her windowes, shall also hearken at her doores.
He that does lodge neere her house, shall also fasten a pin in her walles.
He shall pitch his tent nigh to her, and shall lodge in a lodging where good things are.
He shall set his children under her shelter, and shall lodge under her branches.
By her he shall be couered from heat, and in her glory shall he dwell.
He that feareth the Lord will do good, and he that has the knowledge of the Law shall obtaine her.
And as a mother shall she meet him, and receive him as a wife maried of a virgin.
With the bread of understanding shall she feed him, and give him the water of wisedome to drinke.
He shall be stayed on her, and shall not be moued, and shall rely on her, and shall not be confounded.
She shall exalt him above his neighbours, and in the midst of the congregation shall she open his mouth.
He shall finde ioy, and a crowne of gladnesse, and she shall cause him to inherit an euerlasting name.
But foolish men shall not attaine to her, and sinners shall not see her.
For she is farre from pride, and men that are liers cannot remember her.
Praise is not seemly in the mouth of a sinner, for it was not sent him of the Lord:
For praise shall be vttered in wisdom, and the Lord wil prosper it.
Say not you, It is through the Lord, that I fell away, for you oughtest not to do the things that he hateth.
Say not you, He has caused mee to erre, for he has no need of the sinfull man.
The Lord hateth all abomination, and they that fear Alahayam love it not.
He himself made man from the beginning, and left him in the hand of his counsell,
If you will, to keepe the Commandements, and to performe acceptable faithfulness.
He has set fire and water before you: stretch forth your hand to whether you will.
Before man is life and death, and whether him liketh shall be given him.
For the wisedome of the Lord is great, and he is mighty in power, and beholds all things,
And his eyes are on them that fear him, & he knows every worke of man.
He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man license to sin.
Desire not a multitude of vnprofitable children, neither delight in ungodly sons.
Though they multiply, reioyce not in them, except the fear of the Lord be with them.
Trust not you in their life, neither respect their multitude: for one that is just, is better then a thousand, and better it is to die without children, then to have them that are ungodly.
For by one that has understanding, shall the city be replenished, but the kindred of the wicked, shall speedily become desolate.
Many such things have I seene with mine eyes, and mine eare has heard greater things then these.
In the congregation of the ungodly, shall a fire be kindled, and in a rebellious nation, wrath is set on fire.
He was not pacified towards the old giants, who fell away in the strength of their foolishnesse.
Neither spared he the place where Lot soiourned, but abhorred them for their pride.
He pitied not the people of perdition, who were taken away in their sins.
Nor the six hundreth thousand footmen, who were gathered together in the hardnesse of their hearts.
And if there be one stiffe-necked among the people, it is marueile, if he escape vnpunished; for mercy and wrath are with him, he is mighty to forgiue, and to powre out displeasure.
As his mercy is great, so is his correction also: he iudgeth a man according to his workes.
The sinner shall not escape with his spoiles, and the patience of the godly shall not be frustrate.
Make way for every worke of mercy: for every man shall finde according to his workes.
The Lord hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know him, that his powerfull workes might be knowen to the world.
His mercy is manifest to every creature, and he has separated his light from the darkness with an Adamant.
Say not you, I will hide my self from the Lord: shall any remember me from above? I shall not be remembred among so many people: for what is my soule among such an infinite number of creatures?
Behold, the heaven, and the heaven of heavens, the deepe and the earth, and all that in it is, shall be mooued when he shall visit.
The mountaines also, and foundations of the earth shall be shaken with trembling, when the Lord looketh on them.
No heart can thinke on these things worthily: and who is able to conceiue his ways?
It is a tempest, which no man can see: for the most part of his workes are hidde.
Who can declare the workes of his justice? or who can endure them? for his Couenant is afarre off, and the triall of all things is in the ende.
He that wanteth understanding, will thinke on vaine things: and a foolish man erring, imagineth follies.
My son, hearken to mee, and learne knowledge, and marke my words with your heart.
I will shewe foorth doctrine in weight, and declare his knowledge exactly.
The works of the Lord are done in judgment from the beginning: and from the time he made them, he disposed the parts of it.
He garnished his workes for ever, and in his hand are the chiefe of them to all generations: they neither labour, nor are weary, nor cease from their workes.
None of them hindreth another, and they shall never disobey his word.
After this, the Lord looked on the earth, and filled it with his blessings.
With all maner of living things has he couered the face of it, and they shall returne into it again.
The Lord created man of the earth, and turned him into it again.
He gave them few days, and a short time, and power also over the things in it.
He endued them with strength by themselues, and made them according to his image,
And put the fear of man on all flesh, and gave him dominion over beasts and foules.
Counsell, and a tongue, and eyes, eares, and a heart, gave he them to understand.
Withall, he filled them with the knowledge of understanding, & showed them good and evil.
He set his eye on their hearts, that he might show them the greatness of his workes.
He gave them to glory in his marueilous actes for ever, that they might declare his works with understanding.
And the elect shall praise his holy Name.
Beside this he gave them knowledge, and the law of life for an heritage.
He made an euerlasting couenant with them, and showed them his iudgements.
Their eyes saw the maiestie of his glory, and their eares heard his glorious voyce.
And he said to them, Beware of all vnrighteousnes, and he gave every man commandement concerning his neighbour,
Their ways are ever before him, and shall not be hid from his eyes.
Every man from his youth is given to euil, neither could they make to themselues fleshie hearts for stonie.
For in the diuision of the nations of the whole earth, he set a ruler over every people, but Yahsharala is the Lords portion.
Whom being his first borne, he nourisheth with discipline, and giving him the light of his love, does not forsake him.
Therefore all their workes are as the Sunne before him, and his eyes are continually on their ways.
None of their vnrighteous deeds are hid from him, but all their sins are before the Lord:
But the Lord being gracious, and knowing his workemanship, neither left nor forsooke them, but spared them.
The almes of a man is as a signet with him, and he will keep the good deedes of man, as the apple of the eye, and give repentance to his sons and daughters.
Afterward he will rise up and reward them, and render their recompense on their heads.
But to them that repent, he granted them returne, and comforted those that faile in patience.
Returne to the Lord, and forsake your sins, make your prayer before his face, and offend lesse.
Turne again to the most High, and turne away from iniquitie: for he will leade you out of darkness into the light of health, and hate you abomination vehemently.
Who shall praise the most High in the graue, in stead of them which live and give thanks?
Thankesgiuing perisheth from the dead, as from one that is not: the living and sound in heart, shall praise the Lord.
How great is the louing kindnes of the Lord our Alahayam, and his compassion to such as turne to him in holiness?
For all things cannot be in men, because þ son of man is not immortal.
What is brighter then the Sun? yet the light of it faileth: and flesh and blood will imagine evil.
He vieweth the power of the height of heaven, and all men are but earth and ashes.
He that liueth for ever, created all things in generall.
The Lord only is righteous, and there is none other but he.
Who gouerneth the world with the palme of his hand, and all things obey his will, for he is the king of all, by his power diuiding holy things among them from prophane.
To whom has he given power to declare his works? and who shall finde out his noble actes?
Who shall number the strength of his maiestie? and who shall also tel out his mercies?
As for the wonderous workes of the Lord, there may nothing be taken from them, neither may any thing be put to them, neither can the ground of them be found out.
When a man has done, then he beginneth, and when he leaueth off, then he shall be doubtfull.
What is man, and whereto serueth he? what is his good, & what is his euil?
The number of a mans days at the most are an hundred yeeres.
As a drop of water to the Sea, and a grauell stone in comparison of the sand, so are a thousand yeeres to the days of eternitie.
Therfore is Alahayam patient with them, & powreth forth his mercy on them.
He saw and perceiued their end to be evil, therefore he multiplied his compassion.
The mercy of man is toward his neighbour, but the mercy of the Lord is on all flesh: he reprooueth and nurtureth, and teacheth, & bringeth again as a shepheard his flocke.
He has mercy on them that receive discipline, and that diligently seeke after his iudgements.
My son, blemish not your good deeds, neither use vncomfortable words when you giuest any thing.
Shall not the deaw asswage the heate? so is a word better then a gift.
Loe is not a word better then a gift? but both are with a gracious man.
A foole will vpbraide churlishly, and a gift of the enuious consumeth the eyes.
Learne before you speak, and use phisicke, or ever you be sicke.
Before judgment examine your self, and in the day of visitation you will find mercy.
Humble your self before you be sicke, and in the time of sins show repentance.
Let nothing hinder you to pay your vowe in due time, and deferre not until death to be justified.
Before you prayest, prepare your self, and be not as one that tempteth the Lord.
Thinke on the wrath that shall be at the end; and the time of vengeance when he shall turne away his face.
When you have enough remember the time of hunger, and when you are rich thinke on pouerty and need.
From the morning until the euening the time is changed, and all things are soone done before the Lord.
A wise man will fear in every thing, and in the day of sinning he will beware of offence: but a foole will not obserue time.
Every man of understanding knows wisedome, and wil give praise to him that found her.
They that were of understanding in sayings, became also wise themselues, and powred forth exquisite parables.
Goe not after your lustes, but refraine your self from your appetites.
If you giuest your soule the desires that please her, she will make you a laughing stocke to your enemies, that maligne you.
Take not pleasure in much good cheere, neither be tyed to the expence of it.
Be not made a begger by banquetting on borrowing, when you have nothing in your purse, for you will lie in waite for your own life: and be talked on.
A labouring man that is given to drunkennesse shall not be rich, and he that contemneth small things shall fall by little & little.
Wine and women will make men of understanding to fall away, and he that cleaueth to harlots will become impudent.
Mothes and wormes shall have him to heritage, and a bold man shall be taken away.
He that is hasty to give credit is light minded, and he that sinneth shall offend against his own soule.
Who so takes pleasure in wickednesse shall be condemned, but he that resisteth pleasures, crowneth his life.
He that can rule his tongue shall live without strife, and he that hateth babbling, shall have lesse evil.
Rehearse not to another that which is told to you, and you will fare never the worse.
Whether it be to friend or foe, talk not of other mens liues, and if you canst without offence reueale them not.
For he heard and obserued you, and when time commeth he will hate you.
If you have heard a word, let it die with you, and be bold it will not burst you.
A foole trauaileth with a word, as a woman in labour of a child.
As an arrowe that sticketh in a mans thigh, so is a word within a fooles belly.
Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it, and if he have that he do it no more.
Admonish your friend, it may be he has not said it, and if he have, that he speak it not again.
Admonish a friend: for many times it is a slander, & believe not every tale.
There is one that slippeth in his speach, but not from his heart, and who is he that has not offended with his tongue?
Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him, and not being angry give place to the Law of the most high.
The fear of the Lord is the first step to be accepted and wisedome obtaineth his love.
The knowledge of the Commandements of the Lord, is the doctrine of life, and they that do things that please him, shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortalitie.
The fear of the Lord is all wisedome, and in all wisedome is the performance of the Law, and the knowledge of his omnipotencie.
If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth you, though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.
The knowledge of wickednes is not wisedome, neither at any time the counsell of sinners, prudence.
There is a wickednesse, and the same an abomination, and there is a foole wanting in wisedome.
He that has smal understanding and feareth Alahayam, is better then one that has much wisedome, and transgresseth the Law of the most High.
There is an exquisite subtilty, and the same is vniust, and there is one that turneth aside to make judgment appeare: and there is a wise man that iustifieth in judgment.
There is a wicked man that hangeth down his head sadly; but inwardly he is full of deceit,
Casting down his countenance, and making as if he heard not: where he is not knowen, he will do you a mischiefe before you be aware.
And if for want of power he be hindered from sinning, yet when he findeth opportunitie he wil do euil.
A man may be knowen by his looke, and one that has understanding, by his countenance, when you meetest him.
A mans attire, and excessiue laughter, and gate, show what he is.
There is a reproofe that is not comely: again some man holdeth his tongue, and he is wise.
It is much better to reprooue, then to be angry secretly, and he that confesseth his fault, shall be preserued from hurt.
How good is it when you are reproued, to show repentance? for so will you escape wilfull sin.
As is the lust of an Eunuch to defloure a virgine; so is he that executeth judgment with violence.
There is one that keepeth silence and is found wise: and another by much babling becommeth hatefull.
Some man holdeth his tongue, because he has not to answere, and some keepeth silence, knowing his time.
A wise man wil hold his tongue till he see opportunitie: but a babler and a foole will regard no time.
He that vseth many words shall be abhorred; and he that takes to himself authoritie in it, shall be hated.
There is a sinner that has good successe in evil things; and there is a gaine that turneth to losse.
There is a gift that shall not profit you; and there is a gift whose recompence is double.
There is an abasement because of glory; and there is that lifteth up his head from a low estate.
There is that buyeth much for a little, and repayeth it seven fold.
A wise man by his words makes himself beloued: but the graces of fooles shall be powred out.
The gift of a foole shall do you no good when you have it; neither yet of the enuious for his necessitie: for he looketh to receive many things for one.
He gives little and vpbraideth much; he openeth his mouth like a crier; to day he lendeth, and to morrow will he aske it again: such an one is to be hated of Alahayam and man.
The foole says, I have no friends, I have no thanke for all my good deeds: and they that eate my bread speak evil of me.
How oft, and of how many shall he be laughed to scorne? for he knows not aright what it is to have; and it is all one to him, as if he had it not.
To slip on a pauement, is better then to slip with the tongue: so, the fall of the wicked shall come speedily.
An vnseasonable tale will alwayes be in the mouth of the vnwise.
A wise sentence shall be reiected when it commeth out of a fools mouth: for he will not speak it in due season.
There is that is hindred from sinning through want: and when he takes rest, he shall not be troubled.
There is that destroyeth his own soule through bashfulnesse, and by accepting of persons ouerthroweth himself.
There is that for bashfulnes promiseth to his friend, and makes him his enemy for nothing.
A lie is a foule blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the vntaught.
A thiefe is better then a man that is accustomed to lie: but they both shall have destruction to heritage.
The disposition of a liar is dishonourable, and his shame is ever with him.
A wise man shall promote himself to honour with his words: and he that has understanding, will please great men.
He that tilleth his land, shall increase his heape: and he that pleaseth great men, shall get pardon for iniquity.
Presents and gifts blind the eyes of the wise, and stoppe up his mouth that he cannot reprooue.
Wisedome that is hidde, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?
Better is he that hideth his folly, then a man that hideth his wisedome.
Necessary patience in seeking the Lord, is better then he that leadeth his life without a guide.
My son, have you sinned? do so no more, but aske pardon for your former sins.
Flee from sin as from the face of a Serpent: for if you commest too neere it, it will bite you: the teeth of it, are as the teeth of a lyon, slaying the soules of men.
All iniquitie is as a two edged sword, the wounds whereof cannot be healed.
To terrifie and do wrong, will waste riches: thus the house of proude men shall be made desolate.
A prayer out of a poore mans mouth reacheth to the eares of Alahayam, and his judgment commeth speedily.
He that hateth to be reprooued, is in the way of sinners: but he that feareth the Lord, will repent from his heart.
An eloquent man is knowen farre and neere, but a man of understanding knows when he slippeth.
He that buildeth his house with other mens money, is like one that gathereth himself stones for the tombe of his buriall.
The congregation of the wicked is like tow wrapped together: and the end of them is a flame of fire to destroy them.
The way of sinners is made plaine with stones, but at the ende of it is the pit of hell.
He that keepeth the Law of the Lord, getteth the understanding of it: and the perfection of the fear of the Lord, is wisedome.
He that is not wise, will not be taught: but there is a wisedome which multiplieth bitternesse.
The knowledge of a wise man shall abound like a flood: and his counsell is like a pure fountaine of life.
The inner parts of a foole, are like a broken vessell, and he will holde no knowledge as long as he liueth.
If a skilfull man heare a wise word, he will commend it, and adde to it: but assoone as one of no understanding heareth it, it displeaseth him, and he casteth it behinde his backe.
The talking of a foole is like a burden in the way: but grace shall be found in the lips of the wise.
They inquire at the mouth of the wise man in the congregation, and they shall ponder his words in their heart.
As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisedome to a foole: and the knowledge of the vnwise, is as talke without sense.
Doctrine to fooles, is as fetters on the feete, and like manacles on the right hand.
A foole lifteth up his voyce with laughter, but a wise man does scarce smile a litle.
Learning is to a wise man, as an ornament of gold, and like a bracelet on his right arme.
A foolish mans foote is soone in his house: but a man of experience is ashamed of him.
A foole will peepe in at the doore into the house, but he that is well nurtured, will stand without.
It is the rudenesse of a man to hearken at the doore: but a wise man will be grieued with the disgrace.
The lips of talkers will be telling such things as pertaine not to them: but the words of such as have understanding, are weighed in the ballance.
The heart of fooles is in their mouth, but the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soule.
A whisperer defileth his own soule, and is hated wheresoeuer he dwells.
A slouthful man is compared to a filthy stone, and every one will hisse him out to his disgrace.
A slouthfull man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: every man that takes it up, will shake his hand.
An evil nurtured son is the dishonour of his father that begate him: and a daughter is borne to his losse.
A wise daughter shall bring an inheritance to her husband: but she that liueth dishonestly, is her fathers heauinesse.
She that is bold, dishonoureth both her father and her husband, but they both shall despise her.
A tale out of season musick in mourning: but stripes and correction of wisedome are never out of time.
Who so teacheth a foole, is as one that gleweth a potsheard together, and as he that waketh one from a sound sleepe.
He that telleth a tale to a foole, speaks to one in a slumber: when he has told his tale, he will say, What is the matter?
If children live honestly, and have wherwithall, they shall couer the basenesse of their parents.
But children being haughtie through disdaine, and want of nurture, do staine the nobilitie of their kinred.

Weepe for the dead, for he has lost the light: and weepe for the foole, for he wanteth understanding: make litle weeping for the dead, for he is at rest: but the life of the foole is worse then death.
Seven days do men mourne for him that is dead; but for a foole, and an ungodly man, all the days of his life.

Talke not much with a foole, and goe not to him that has no understanding, beware of him lest you have trouble, and you will never be defiled with his fooleries: depart from him, and you will find rest, and never be disquieted with madnesse.
What is heauier then lead? and what is the name of it, but a foole?
Sand, and salt, and a masse of yron is easier to beare then a man without understanding.
As timber girt and bound together in a building, cannot be loosed with shaking: so the heart that is stablished by aduised counsel, shall fear at no time.
A heart setled on a thought of understanding, is as a faire plaistering on the wall of a gallerie.
Pales set on an high place will never stand against the wind: so a feareful heart in the imagination of a foole, can not stand against any fear.
He that pricketh the eye, wil make teares to fall: and he that pricketh the heart, makes it to shewe her knowledge.
Who so casteth a stone at the birds, frayeth them away, and he that vpbraideth his friend, breaketh friendship.
Though you drewest a sword at your friend, yet despaire not, for there way be a returning (to favor.)

If you have opened your mouth against your friend, fear not, for there may be a reconciliation: except for vpbraiding, or pride, or disclosing of secrets, or a treacherous wound, for, for these things every friend will depart.

Be faithfull to your neighbour in his pouertie, that you mayest reioyce in his prosperitie: abide stedfast to him in the time of his trouble, that you mayest be heire with him in his heritage: for a meane estate is not alwayes to be contemned, nor the rich that is foolish, to be had in admiration.
As the vapour and smoke of a furnace goes before the fire: so reuiling before blood.
I will not be ashamed to defend a friend: neither will I hide my self from him.
And if any evil happen to me by him, every one that heareth it will beware of him.
Who shall set a watch before my mouth, and a seale of wisedome on my lippes, that I fall not suddenly by them, & that my tongue destroy me not?
O Lord, father and gouernour of all my whole life, leaue me not to their counsels, and let me not fall by them.
Who will set scourges over my thoughts, and the discipline of wisedome over mine heart? that they spare me not for mine ignorances and it passe not by my sins:
Least mine ignorances increase, and my sins abound to my destruction, and I fall before mine aduersaries, and mine enemie reioyce over mee, whose hope is farre from your mercy.
O Lord, father and Alahayam of my life, give me not a proud looke, but turne away from your servants alwaies a haughty mind:
Turne away from mee vaine hopes, and concupiscence, and you will hold him up that is desirous alwaies to serve you.
Let not the greedinesse of the belly, nor lust of the flesh take hold of me, and give not over me your servant into an impudent mind.
Heare, O you children, the discipline of the mouth: He that keepeth it, shall never be taken in his lippes.
The sinner shall be left in his foolishnesse: both the evil speaker and the proud shall fall thereby.
Accustome not your mouth to swearing: neither use your self to the naming of the holy one.
For as a servant that is continually beaten, shall not be without a blew marke: so he that sweareth and nameth Alahayam continually, shall not be faultlesse.

A man that vseth much swearing shall be filled with iniquity, and the plague shall never depart from his house: If he shall offend, his sin shall be on him: and if he acknowledge not his sin, he makes a double offence, and if he sweare in vaine, he shall not be innocent, but his house shall be full of calamities.

There is a word that is clothed about with death: Alahayam graunt that it be not found in the heritage of Jacob, for all such things shall be farre from the godly, and they shall not wallow in their sins.
Use not your mouth to vntemperate swearing, for in it is the word of sin.

Remember your father and your mother, when you sittest among great men. Be not forgetfull before them, and so you by your custome become a foole, and wish that you hadst not been borne, and curse the day of your natiuitie.
The man that is accustomed to opprobrious words, will never be reformed all the daies of his life.

Two sorts of men multiply sin, and the third will bring wrath: a hot mind is as a burning fire, it will never be quenched till it be consumed: a fornicatour in the body of his flesh, will never cease till he has kindled a fire.
All bread is sweete to a whoremonger, he will not leaue off till he die.

A man that breaketh wedlocke, saying thus in his heart, Who seeth me? I am compassed about with darknesse: the walles couer me; & no body seeth me, what neede I to fear? The most high wil not remember my sins:

Such a man only feareth the eies of men, and knows not that the eies of the Lord are tenne thousand times brighter then the Sunne, beholding all the waies of men, and considering the most secret parts.
He knew all things ere ever they were created, so also after they were perfited, he looked on them all:
This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, and where he suspecteth not, he shall be taken.
Thus shall it goe also with the wife, that leaueth her husband, and bringeth in an heire by another:
For first she has disobeyed the Law of the most High: and secondly, she has trespassed against her own husband, and thirdly, she has played the whore in adultery, and brought children by another man.
She shall be brought out into the congregation, and inquisition shall be made of her children.
Her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring foorth no fruit.
She shall leaue her memorie to be cursed, and her reproch shall not be blotted out.
And they that remaine, shall know that there is nothing better then the fear of the Lord, and that there is nothing sweeter then to take heed to the Commandement of the Lord.
It is great glory to follow the Lord, & to be received of him is long life.
Wisedome shall praise her self, and shall glory in the midst of her people.
In the Congregation of the most high, shall she open her mouth, and triumph before his power.
I came out of the mouth of the most High, and couered the earth as a cloud.
I dwelt in high places, and my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
I alone compassed the circuit of heaven, and walked in the bottome of the deepe.
In the waues of the sea, and in all the earth, and in every people, and nation, I got a possession.
With all these I sought rest: and in whose inheritance shall I abide?
So the creatour of all things gave mee a commandement, and he that made me, caused my tabernacle to rest: and said, Let your dwelling be in Jacob, and your inheritance in Yahsharala.
He created mee from the beginning before the world, and I shall never faile.
In the holy Tabernacle I serued before him: and so was I established in Sion.
Likewise in the beloued city he gave mee rest, and in Jerusalem was my power.
And I tooke roote in an honourable people, even in the portion of the Lords inheritance.
I was exalted like a Cedar in Libanus, and as a Cypresse tree on the mountaines of Hermon.
I was exalted like a palme tree in Engaddi, and as a rose-plant in Iericho, as a faire oliue tree in a pleasant fielde, and grew up as a planetree by the water.
I gave a sweete smell like cinamon, and aspalathus, and I yeelded a pleasant odour like the best mirrhe, as Galbanum and Onix, and sweet Storax, and as the sume of franckincense in the Tabernacle.
As the Turpentine tree, I stretched out my branches, and my branches are the branches of honour and grace.
As the Uine brought I foorth pleasant sauour, and my flowers are the fruit of honour and riches.
I am the mother of faire love, and fear, and knowledge, and holy hope, I therefore being eternall, am given to all my children which are named of him.
Come to me all you that be desirous of mee, and fill your selues with my fruits.
For my memorial is sweeter then hony, and mine inheritance then the hony combe.
They that eate mee shall yet be hungry, and they that drinke me shall yet be thirstie.
He that obeyeth me, shall never be confounded, and they that worke by me, shall not do amisse.
All these things are the book of the Couenant of the most high Alahayam, even the Law which Moses commanded for an heritage to the Congregations of Jacob.
Faint not to be strong in the Lord; that he may confirme you, cleaue to him: for the Lord Almightie is Alahayam alone, and besides him there is no other Savior.
He filleth all things with his wisdom, as Physon, and as Tigris in the time of the new fruits.
He makes the understanding to abound like Euphrates, and as Iorden in the time of the haruest.
He makes the doctrine of knowledge appeare as the light, and as Geon in the time of vintage.
The first man knew her not perfectly: no more shall the last finde her out.
For her thoughts are more then the Sea, and her counsels profounder then the great deepe.
I also came out as a brooke from a riuer, and as a conduit into a garden.
I said, I will water my best garden, and will water abundantly my garden bedde: and loe, my brooke became a riuer, and my riuer became a sea.
I will yet make doctrine to shine as the morning, and will send forth her light afarre off.
I will yet powre out doctrine as prophecie, and leaue it to all ages for ever.
Behold that I have not laboured for my self only, but for all them that seeke wisedome.
In three things I was beautified, and stoode up beautiful, both before Alahayam and men: the vnitie of brothers, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.
Three sorts of men my soule hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poore man that is proud, a rich man that is a lyar, and an old adulterer that doteth.
If you have gathered nothing in your youth, how canst you finde any thing in your age?
Oh how comely a thing is judgment for gray haires, and for ancient men to know counsell?
Oh how comely is the wisedome of old men, and understanding and counsell to men of honour?
Much experience is the crowne of old men, and the fear of Alahayam is their glory.
There be nine things which I have iudged in mine heart to be happy, and the tenth I will vtter with my tongue: a man that has ioy of his children, and he that liueth to see the fall of his enemie.
Well is him that dwells with a wife of understanding, and that has not slipped with his tongue, and that has not serued a man more vnworthy then himself.
Well is him that has found prudence, and he that speaks in the eares of him that will heare.
Oh how great is he that findeth wisedome! yet is there none above him that feareth the Lord.
But the love of the Lord passeth all things for illumination: he that holdeth it, whereto shall he be likened?
The fear of the Lord is the beginning of his love: and faith is the beginning of cleauing to him.
any plague, but the plague of the heart: and any wickednesse, but the wickednesse of a woman.
And any affliction, but the affliction from them that hate me: and any revenge, but the revenge of enemies.
There is no head above the head of a serpent, and there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemie.
I had rather dwell with a lyon and a dragon, then to keepe house with a wicked woman.
The wickednesse of a woman changeth her face, and darkeneth her countenance like sackecloth.
Her husband shall sit among his neighbours: and when he heareth it, shall sigh bitterly.
All wickednesse is but little to the wickednesse of a woman: let the portion of a sinner fall on her.
As the climbing up a sandie way is to the feete of the aged, so is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
Stumble not at the beautie of a woman, and desire her not for pleasure.
A woman, if she maintaine her husband, is full of anger, impudencie, and much reproch.
A wicked woman abateth the courage, makes a heauie countenance, and a wounded heart: a woman that will not comfort her husband in distresse makes weake hands, and feeble knees.
Of the woman came the beginning of sin, & through her we all die.
Give the water no passage: neither a wicked woman libertie to gad abroad.
If she goe not as you would have her, cut her off from your flesh, and give her a bill of diuorce, and let her goe.
Blessed is the man that has a vertuous wife, for the number of his days shall be double.
A vertuous woman reioyceth her husband, and he shall fulfill the yeeres of his life in peace.
A good wife is a good portion, which shall be given in the portion of them that fear the Lord.
Whether a man be rich or poore, if he have a good heart towards the Lord, he shall at all times reioyce with a cheerefull countenance.

There be three things that mine heart feareth: and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an vnruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse then death.
But a griefe of heart and sorrow, is a woman that is ielous over another woman, and a scourge of the tongue which communicateth withall.
An euil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro: he that has hold of her, is as though he held a scorpion.
A drunken woman and a gadder abroad, causeth great anger, and she will not couer her own shame.
The whordome of a woman may be knowen in her haughtie lookes, and eye lids.
If your daughter be shamelesse, keepe her in straitly: lest she abuse her self through ouermuch libertie.
Watch over an impudent eye: and marueile not, if she trespasse against you.
She will open her mouth as a thirstie traueiler, when he has found a fountaine: and drinke of every water neere her: by every hedge will she sit down, and open her quiuer against every arrow.
The grace of a wife delighteth her husband, and her discretion will fat his bones.
A silent and louing woman is a gift of the Lord, and there is nothing so much worth, as a mind well instructed.
A shamefast and faithfull woman is a double grace, and her continent mind cannot be valued.
As the Sunne when it ariseth in the high heaven: so is the beautie of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
As the cleare light is on the holy candlesticke: so is the beautie of the face in ripe age.
As the golden pillars are on the sockets of siluer: so are the faire feete with a constant heart.
My son, keepe the flowre of your age sound: and give not your strength to strangers.
When you have gotten a fruitfull possession through all the field: sowe it with your own seede, trusting in the goodness of your stocke.
So your race which you leauest shall be magnified, hauing the confidence of their good descent.
An harlot shall be accounted as spittle: but a maried woman is a towre against death to her husband.
A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man: but a godly woman is given to him that feareth the Lord.
A dishonest woman contemneth shame, but an honest woman will reuerence her husband.
A shamelesse woman shall be counted as a dog: but she that is shamefast will fear the Lord.
A woman that honoureth her husband, shall be iudged wise of all: but she that dishonoureth him in her pride, shall be counted ungodly of all.
A loude crying woman, and a scolde, shall be sought out to driue away the enemies.

There be two things that grieue my heart: and the third makes me angry: a man of warre that suffereth pouerty, and men of understanding that are not set by: and one that returneth from righteousness to sin: the Lord prepareth such a one for the sword.
A merchant shall hardly keepe himself from doing wrong: and an huckster shall not be freed from sin.
Many have sinned for a smal matter: & he that seeks for abundance will turne his eies away.
As a naile sticketh fast between the ioynings of the stones: so does sin sticke close between buying and selling.
Unlesse a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soone be ouerthrowen.
As when one sifteth with a sieue, the refuse remaineth, so the filth of man in his talke.
The furnace prooueth the potters vessell: so the triall of man is in his reasoning.
The fruite declareth if the tree have been dressed: so is the vtterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
Praise no man before you hearest him speak, for this is the triall of men.
If you followest righteousness, you will obtaine her, and put her on, as a glorious long robe.
The birds will resort to their like, so will truth returne to them that practise in her.
As the Lyon lieth in waite for the pray: so sin for them that worke iniquity.
The discourse of a godly man is alwaies with wisedome: but a foole changeth as the Moone.
If you be among the vndiscreet, obserue the time: but be continually among men of understanding.
The discourse of fooles is irksome, and their sport is in the wantonnesse of sin.
The talke of him that sweareth much, makes the haire stand vpright: and their braules make one stop his eares.
The strife of the proud is blood-shedding, and their reuilings are grieuous to the eare.
Who so discouereth secrets, looseth his credit: and shall never find friend to his mind.
Love your friend, and be faithfull to him: but if you bewrayest his secrets, follow no more after him.
For as a man has destroyed his enemie: so have you lost the love of your neighbour.
As one that letteth a bird goe out of his hand, so have you let your neighbour goe; and will not get him again.
